names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 9 noiembrie, «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan Colov»; the bare personal name, without the epithet.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 9 Νοεμβρίου, «Όσιος Ιωάννης ο Βραχύσωμος ή Κολοβός», with the rank word left off.

The forename and the by-name of the calendar's name page heading, «Иоанн Колов, Младший, Скитский, отшельник», with the rank word and the page's two further by-names left off; the day's line prints the same two words in the genitive, «Прп. Иоанна Колова».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 9. новембар ст. ст., „Преп. Јован Колов.“ — «Преп.» is the `venerable` grade `types` keeps and comes off, while «Колов» stays: it is a by-name and not a rank, and the entry’s own second sentence explains it, «Колов – означава Мали», Colobos means the Little, because he was small of stature. That is the fullest bare form the heading gives and it is what keeps him apart from the other Johns. The Russian form already stored writes «Иоанн Колов».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 9 ноября ст. ст. — «Прп. Иоанна Колова (V).»
doxologia.ro, calendarul pentru 9 noiembrie — «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan Colov»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 9ης Νοεμβρίου — «Όσιος Ιωάννης ο Βραχύσωμος ή Κολοβός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 9 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same man: the short-bodied ascetic of the Egyptian desert, called Kolobos for his stature. The page gives no year, so no `dates` object is proposed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence, and it prints no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.11.2025 (9. новембар ст. ст.) — „Преп. Јован Колов.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. `dates` UNTOUCHED: the entry gives no year at all, so the fifth century this folder holds from its other calendars stands. The three other saints its body names — his teacher, his pupil and his fellow-pupil — are all folders this one ALREADY related to in both directions, so the life links them and no `related` row was added or owed. His brother, who came with him to Scetis and had to hold back his zeal, is named in the book and is NOT named in the life: he has no folder, and the bare forename would have read as one of the corpus’s other men of that name.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru's life for him: «подвизался в египетской пустыне в V веке», and the day's line closes «(V)». The first date this folder has carried.
